segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: Let’s finalize the release plan. Are we still comfortable targeting Friday?

segments.speaker: Ahmed
segments.text: Yes. Backend work is mostly complete, but final QA still needs to happen before production.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: Then Friday stays as the target release date as long as QA is completed by Thursday at 5 PM.

segments.speaker: Ahmed
segments.text: Agreed. I’ll own the final backend testing and finish it by Thursday at 5 PM.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: I’ll prepare the deployment checklist and release notes by Thursday afternoon.

segments.speaker: Ahmed
segments.text: One concern is the mobile meeting summary screen. The latest build still has a layout issue.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: Let’s treat that as a release blocker. Can you fix it by Wednesday evening?

segments.speaker: Ahmed
segments.text: Yes. I’ll fix the mobile layout issue by Wednesday evening and send the updated build.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: For rollout, let’s start with 10 percent of users and monitor errors for a few hours.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: We should also watch completion rates and session errors during the first rollout.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: If those metrics stay normal, we can expand to the full user base the same day.

segments.speaker: Ahmed
segments.text: I’ll monitor production logs after deployment and flag anything unusual.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: Search should work across meeting titles and transcript content for the first release.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Public sharing should remain read-only and should not require login.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: Yes. We’ll expose only the recap, action items, and highlights behind an unguessable share token.

segments.speaker: Saeed
segments.text: Main priority is still the core meeting experience. Extra integrations can wait.
